stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the modern cell theory?
option_a: All living things are made of cells.
option_b: Cells are the basic unit of structure and function in living things.
option_d: All cells come from pre-existing cells.
explanation: Prokaryotic cells such as bacteria have no nucleus, so "all cells contain a nucleus" is not part of the cell theory. The other three are.

stem: The modern cell theory states that new cells come from
explanation: New cells come only from cells that already exist, by cell division. Spontaneous generation (life from nonliving material) was disproven.

stem: What is the smallest unit of life that can carry out all life processes?
explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out every life process. An organelle is only part of a cell; tissues and organs are made of many cells.

stem: Why is the cell considered the basic unit of life?
option_a: It can perform all life functions independently.
option_b: It is smaller than an atom.
option_d: It exists only in multicellular organisms.
explanation: A single cell can take in energy, grow, respond, and reproduce on its own. Cells are much larger than atoms, and single-celled organisms are cells too.

stem: You are designing an experiment to test whether a substance is living. What observation would support that it follows the cell theory?
option_a: It is made of organized cells that reproduce.
explanation: The cell theory says living things are made of cells and cells come from other cells. Changing color or reacting with acid happens to nonliving things too.

stem: Why can eukaryotic cells perform more complex functions than prokaryotic cells?
explanation: Membrane-bound organelles let a eukaryotic cell split jobs into separate compartments. Both cell types have ribosomes and DNA, and eukaryotic cells are usually larger.

stem: You are given two unknown cells. One has a nucleus and mitochondria; the other does not. How would you classify them?
explanation: A nucleus and membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria mean eukaryotic. A cell without them is prokaryotic.

stem: The DNA of a prokaryotic cell is located in the
explanation: Prokaryotes have no nucleus, so their DNA sits in the cytoplasm (in a region called the nucleoid).

stem: Which of the following cell types does NOT have a nucleus?
explanation: Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus. Plant and animal cells are eukaryotic, and eukaryotic means "true nucleus."

stem: Which of the following is an example of a prokaryotic cell?
explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes. Fungi, animals, and plants are all made of eukaryotic cells.

stem: Match each cell part with its job.
option_a: Nucleus :: Controls cell activity and contains genetic material
option_b: Nuclear membrane :: Controls movement in and out of the nucleus
option_c: Mitochondria :: Produces usable energy for the cell (ATP)
option_d: Lysosome :: Breaks down particles and digests old cell parts; contains enzymes
explanation: The nucleus is the control center and holds DNA; the nuclear membrane controls what enters and leaves it; mitochondria make ATP; lysosomes digest with enzymes; ribosomes build proteins.

stem: Match each cell part with its job.
option_a: Nucleolus :: Center of the nucleus where ribosomes are made
option_b: Cell membrane :: Supports, protects, and controls movement of material in and out of the cell
option_c: Cell wall :: Rigid outer structure found in plants and bacteria
option_d: Chloroplast :: Converts energy from the sun to make sugar
option_e: Endoplasmic reticulum :: Transports materials throughout the cell; has smooth and rough portions
explanation: The nucleolus makes ribosomes; the cell membrane controls what goes in and out; the cell wall is the rigid layer of plants and bacteria; chloroplasts capture sunlight to make sugar; the ER is the cell's transport network.

stem: Match each cell part with its job.
option_a: Cytoskeleton :: Structural proteins that help the cell keep its shape
option_b: Cytoplasm :: Jelly-like material that supports and protects cell organelles
option_c: Cilia :: Hair-like projections on the surface of cells
option_d: Vacuole :: Stores food, water, and waste
option_e: Golgi apparatus :: Modifies, packages, and labels proteins
explanation: The cytoskeleton is the cell's frame; cytoplasm is the jelly the organelles sit in; cilia are tiny hairs on the surface; vacuoles store materials; the Golgi packages and ships proteins.

stem: Identify the organelle indicated by the arrow.
explanation: The arrow points to the large purple sphere in the center: the nucleus, which holds the cell's DNA.

stem: Identify the organelle indicated by the arrow.
explanation: The arrow points to the folded membranes wrapped around the nucleus, dotted with ribosomes: the rough endoplasmic reticulum. Smooth ER has no ribosomes.

stem: Identify the organelle indicated by the arrow.
explanation: The arrow points to the thin outer boundary of an animal cell: the cell membrane. Animal cells have no cell wall.

stem: Identify the organelle indicated by the arrow.
explanation: The arrow points to the bean-shaped organelle with folded inner membranes: a mitochondrion, which makes ATP.

stem: Identify the organelle indicated by the arrow.
explanation: The arrow points to the stack of flattened, curved sacs: the Golgi apparatus, which packages and ships proteins.

stem: The cell membrane functions
option_a: to regulate what goes into and out of a cell
explanation: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves, and it also supports and protects the cell, so all three are its jobs.

stem: What is the main structure in this image?
stimulus_text: Use the picture of a section of cell membrane to answer the next two questions.
explanation: The picture shows a phospholipid bilayer with proteins in it: the cell membrane.

stem: The blue structures in this image are
explanation: The large blue shapes that stretch across or sit in the membrane are proteins. The orange heads with tails are the phospholipids.

stem: The blue circles are water molecules and the red circles are glucose molecules. The membrane in the middle lets water through but not glucose. What would you expect to happen?
option_a: Glucose molecules will diffuse to the right
option_b: Glucose molecules will diffuse to the left
option_c: Water molecules will diffuse to the right
option_d: Water molecules will diffuse to the left
explanation: There is more water on the left and more glucose on the right. Water moves by osmosis from where it is more concentrated (left) to where it is less concentrated (right).

stem: Why is the dialysis bag on the left blue/black?
option_a: Starch went out of the bag
option_c: Iodine went out of the bag
option_d: Iodine went into the bag and reacted with starch
explanation: Iodine is small enough to pass through the dialysis tubing. Inside the bag it met starch, and iodine turns starch blue-black. Starch is too big to leave the bag.

stem: If a substance is spread evenly throughout a space, the substance
explanation: When the concentration is the same everywhere, there is no gradient, so there is no net movement: the substance is at equilibrium.

stem: When mixing Kool-Aid, the solvent is
explanation: The solvent is what does the dissolving, which is water. The sugar and drink mix are the solutes.

stem: Osmosis is best described as
option_a: the movement of sugar across a membrane
option_b: the movement of salt across a membrane
option_c: the movement of water across a membrane
explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane.

stem: Which of the following is true for active transport?
option_c: It moves molecules from low concentration to high.
explanation: Active transport pumps molecules against their gradient (low to high), using transport proteins and energy from ATP.

stem: Which of the following is an example of passive transport?
option_d: All of the above are examples of passive transport
explanation: Passive transport needs no energy because molecules move from high to low concentration. Simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion, and osmosis are all passive.

stem: Which of the following types of transport requires a transport protein?
explanation: Facilitated diffusion uses a channel or carrier protein, and active transport uses protein pumps. Simple diffusion and osmosis can happen straight through the membrane.

stem: What would happen to a fish from the ocean if it was placed in freshwater?
option_a: Water would move out of its cells, the cells would shrivel up, and it would die.
option_b: Too much water would move into its cells, and it would die.
option_c: Salt would move in and out.
option_d: The fish would live because it is in equilibrium.
explanation: Ocean fish cells are saltier than freshwater, so freshwater is hypotonic to them. Water rushes into the cells by osmosis, and they swell and can burst.

stem: Which of the following molecules was NOT able to pass through the dialysis tubing in the diffusion lab?
option_e: All were able to pass through
explanation: Starch molecules are too large to fit through the tubing's pores. Water, glucose, and iodine are small enough to pass.

stem: Which beaker shows a cell in a hypertonic environment?
stimulus_text: Each beaker holds a cell that is 10% salt inside. Beaker A is 10% salt, Beaker B is 2% salt, and Beaker C is 30% salt. Use the picture to answer the next two questions.
explanation: A hypertonic solution has more solute than the cell. Beaker C (30% salt) is saltier than the cell (10%), so water leaves the cell.

stem: Which cell would you expect to increase in size?
explanation: Beaker B (2% salt) is hypotonic to the cell (10%), so water moves into the cell and it swells.

stem: Identical pieces of potato are placed in sucrose solutions of different concentrations. After three hours, the mass of each potato piece is measured. Which graph represents the expected results?
explanation: The more sucrose in the solution, the more water leaves the potato by osmosis, so the mass goes down as concentration goes up (Graph D).

stem: What unit was used for the dependent variable?
stimulus_text: Cells with different starting concentrations were placed in a 0.4 M salt solution, and each cell's final mass was measured. Use the graph to answer the next four questions.
explanation: The dependent variable is mass, on the y-axis, measured in grams.

stem: What was the final mass of the cell with a 0.8 M concentration?
explanation: Find 0.8 on the x-axis and read up to the point: 15 grams.

stem: What would be the final mass of a cell starting with a 0.6 M concentration?
explanation: Find 0.6 on the x-axis and read up to the point: 11 grams.

stem: The cell with a 0.6 M starting concentration would be in what type of solution?
explanation: The cell (0.6 M) is more concentrated than the 0.4 M salt solution around it, so the solution is hypotonic to the cell. Water moves in, which is why its mass went up.
